name: Honor del Bazacle (Bazacle milling company, Toulouse)
exchange: Toulouse (notarial / company-register transfers; Bourse de Toulouse from 1887; Paris listing 1910)
top10_years: 1372-1601 (only priced company); plausibly top 10 to c.1690; later appearances in top10.csv only reflect how few companies are priced
notes: Grain milling (consumer/food) 1372-1888; electricity generation (industrial) from 1888. Values in kg of fine silver (currency XAG_KG, value column = millions of kg) because the source reports prices in silver; multiply by ~GBP8.98/kg (111.4 g fine silver per GBP, 1601-1816) or a silver price series. Uchaux: 80 (1372), 88 (1374), 96 (1384), 100 (1535), 128 (1714), 136 (1804). Gap 1451-1522; register for 1817-1853 lost. Tiny (0.5-4 tonnes of silver) but the oldest priced company.

name: Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie (Dutch East India Company)
confidence: high 1602-1698 and 1719-20; low 1721-1795 (read off GFD chart)
notes: Paid-in capital f6,424,588 (Van Dillen/Gaastra; Petram cites Den Heijer f6,429,588), never increased; price = % of par for Amsterdam-chamber shares, applied to whole capital. Nationalised 1 Mar 1796 by the Batavian Republic, charter lapsed 31 Dec 1799. Real peak Aug 1720 (1,210% = f77.7m), not 1637. No price data 1699-1718 (GFD interpolates).

name: Geoctrooieerde West-Indische Compagnie (first Dutch West India Company)
notes: Charter 1621, capital f7,108,161 raised by 1623, increased by calls to ~f17m by 1639 (Odegard). Prices 1628-1650 read off the GFD WIC1-AM chart; unclear if quoted on original or paid-in capital, so est_low/est_high. No prices 1651-1674. Bankrupt; restructured 1674 into the second WIC (old shares got 15% in new stock after paying 4%; creditors 30%).

name: Second Dutch West India Company (Geoctrooieerde West-Indische Compagnie, 1674)
notes: Nominal capital f6,332,362 (Schneeloch, final 1710) / f4,505,863 (Den Heijer, initial); traded below par except 1688 and 1720. 1720 subscriptions not included. Charter not renewed 1791; company taken over by the States General.

name: East India Company (Governor and Company of Merchants of London trading into the East Indies)
aka: United Company of Merchants of England Trading to the East Indies (1709); Honourable East India Company
notes: Separate voyages 1601-1612, terminable joint stocks 1613-1656, permanent New General Stock 1657. In 1709 the Old Company united with the English Company (eic_english); legally the United Company grew out of the 1698 English Company charter, but id eic is kept for the continuous enterprise. Capital GBP3,163,000 (1709), 3,194,080 (1718), 4m (1786), 5m (1789), 6m (1794; Fortune 1817 confirms 6m). Trade monopoly ended 1813/1833, government of India to the Crown 1858, stock redeemed and company dissolved 1874.

name: English Company Trading to the East Indies ("New Company")
notes: Formed from the GBP2m loan of 1698; its stock GBP1,662,000. Briefly worth more than the Old Company (1700-1705).

name: Governor and Company of the Bank of England
Governor and Company of the Merchants of Great Britain trading to the South Seas (South Sea Company)
notes: In substance a holder of government debt. Capital 9,177,968 (1711), 10m (1715), 11,746,844 (1719); 1720 conversions and money subscriptions took issued stock to ~18.5m by May 1720 and authorised stock to 37.8m; ~32-33.8m after the 1721 readjustment; half turned into South Sea Annuities 1723; trading stock GBP3,662,784 from 1733 (Fortune 1817). Dissolved 1853 (stock converted into government annuities).

name: Compagnie d'Occident (1717) / Compagnie des Indes (1719)
aka: Mississippi Company; Compagnie perpetuelle des Indes; absorbed the Banque Royale (Feb 1720)
notes: Values in livres tournois (FRF), largely in depreciating Banque Royale notes in 1720 - convert with the monthly exchange rates given in the notes. Shares: 200,000 (1717-18), 250,000 (Jun 1719), 300,000 (Jul 1719) + 300,000 partly paid subscriptions (Sep-Oct 1719), 600,000 (12 Mar 1720), 200,000 (3 Jun 1720), 56,000 after the 1721 Visa. Trade monopoly suspended 1769; liquidation finished in the 1790s.

name: Royal African Company of England
notes: Capital 111,100 (1672), 444,400 (1691), 625,250 (1693), 1,101,050 (1697), written down to 451,350 in the 1712 reconstruction. Slave-trading company. Dissolved 1752 (assets to the Company of Merchants Trading to Africa).

name: Million Bank (Bank on Tickets of the Million Adventure)
notes: Capital GBP500,000 (Scott). Founded 1695 to hold Million Adventure lottery tickets; wound up 1796 with a surplus.

name: Royal Exchange Assurance Corporation
notes: Nominal stock GBP1,152,000 then 1,212,000 with 10% paid; reorganised Oct 1720 into 12,120 shares of GBP50 (GBP10 paid). Quotes are per GBP100 nominal stock.

name: London Assurance Corporation
notes: 19,740 shares with GBP5 called by Sept 1720 (Scott); earlier 1720 share count uncertain. Acquired by Sun Alliance 1965.

name: Governor and Company of Adventurers of England trading into Hudson's Bay
notes: Capital 10,500 (1670), 31,500 (1690), 103,950 (1720). Tiny before 1825. Fate after 1825 for era-B/D researchers to confirm (taken private 2008 and 2020; creditor protection and liquidation 2025).

name: Bank of the United States (First)
notes: Capital $10m (25,000 x $400); only par value recorded here. Charter expired 1811.

name: Second Bank of the United States
notes: Capital $35m (350,000 x $100); price "around $120 for over a decade" (MoAF). Federal charter expired 1836; Pennsylvania successor failed 1841. Era-B researcher should replace with dated quotes.

name: Banque de France
notes: 30,000 shares of 1,000 F (1800), 45,000 (1803), 90,000 (1806), 67,900 after 1818-20 buybacks. No price series collected (see Manas 2019).
